settings.heading: Why a phone,
settings.text:
I taught camera courses for eight years. Every time, people went home with a heavy bag and took their best pictures on their phone anyway.

So this course starts with the camera you carry. Light, framing and timing matter far more than the lens, and a phone is the one you have with you when the light is good.

Four weeks, twenty minutes a day. You will look at light differently by the end of the first week.
settings.name: Teo Varga
settings.role: Photographer and teacher. Write your own letter here.

settings.question: Which phone do I need?
settings.answer: Any phone from the last five years. Every lesson works on both kinds of phone, and nothing needs the newest model.

settings.question: Do I need to buy an editing app?
settings.answer: No. The editing lessons and presets use free apps that come with your phone or cost nothing.

settings.question: How much time does it take?
settings.answer: About twenty minutes a day: a short lesson and a few pictures. You can pause and pick it up a week later.

settings.question: How do the live critiques work?
settings.answer: Post your best picture of the week by Wednesday. On Thursday evening Teo looks at them on a video call. Recordings stay in the course.

settings.question: What if it is not for me?
settings.answer: Write within 30 days and you get every cent back. Replace this with your own terms.
